title_en: The 80/20 Portfolio, Bipartisan Stocks and Slumpy Septembers
title_zh: 80/20投资组合、两党共持的股票与低迷的九月
subtitle_zh: 彭博《万亿》（Trillions）播客：主持人乔尔·韦伯（Joel Weber）与埃里克·巴尔丘纳斯（Eric Balchunas）对话彭博行业研究ETF分析师阿萨纳西奥斯·普萨罗法吉斯（Athanasios Psarofagis）和彭博新闻记者伊莎贝尔·李（Isabelle Lee），解读ETF资产为何从60/40演变为80/20、追踪国会议员交易的政治主题ETF（NANC与GOP），以及债券型共同基金潜藏的'死亡循环'风险。
description: The 80/20 Portfolio, Bipartisan Stocks and Slumpy Septembers

speakers.1: Joel Weber（乔尔·韦伯）— 主持人，彭博
speakers.2: Eric Balchunas（埃里克·巴尔丘纳斯）— 主持人，彭博行业研究（Bloomberg Intelligence）高级ETF分析师
speakers.3: Athanasios Psarofagis（阿萨纳西奥斯·普萨罗法吉斯，节目中昵称 Ethan/伊森）— 嘉宾，彭博行业研究ETF分析师（原ASR误作 'Sarafegas'）
speakers.4: Isabelle Lee（伊莎贝尔·李）— 嘉宾，彭博新闻（Bloomberg News）跨资产/市场记者（原ASR误作 'Isabel Lee'）
speakers.5: Announcer — 彭博音频工作室（Bloomberg Audio Studios）片头播报

turns.en: Bloomberg Audio Studios.
turns.zh: 彭博音频工作室（Bloomberg Audio Studios）。

turns.en: Podcasts. Radio.
turns.zh: 播客。电台。

turns.en: News.
turns.zh: 新闻。

turns.en: We've looked at performance of Nance and GOP. And as you can imagine, when there was a Democratic president, Nance was doing better. And now GOP is doing slightly better. But I think where it gets interesting is there are names that are held by both.
turns.zh: 我们研究了NANC和GOP这两只ETF的表现。可想而知，当总统是民主党人时，NANC表现更好；而现在GOP略胜一筹。但我觉得真正有意思的地方在于，有一些股票是两党都持有的。

turns.en: Wait, there's a middle?
turns.zh: 等等，还有中间地带？

turns.en: And if you just build a basket of those, you end up beating everything else.
turns.zh: 而如果你就把这些股票打包成一个组合，最后它的表现会跑赢其他所有组合。

turns.en: Welcome to Trillions. I'm Joel Weber.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听《万亿》（Trillions）。我是乔尔·韦伯（Joel Weber）。

turns.en: And I'm Eric Balchunas.
turns.zh: 我是埃里克·巴尔丘纳斯（Eric Balchunas）。

turns.en: Eric, we are experimenting with some new formats. This episode is going to be no exception. One of the members of your team who's been a regular on the show is Athanasios Sarafegas, who's an ETF analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence. There's been a few themes of late that Ethan and I discussed previously, and we wanted to create an episode that we can come back to again and again with Ethan and Isabel Lee, cross-asset reporter from Bloomberg News. to kind of like do a little spotlight episode on a few of these themes and research notes.
turns.zh: 埃里克，我们正在尝试一些新的节目形式，这一期也不例外。你团队里有一位常客，就是彭博行业研究（Bloomberg Intelligence）的ETF分析师阿萨纳西奥斯·普萨罗法吉斯（Athanasios Psarofagis）。最近有几个主题，伊森（Ethan）和我之前讨论过，我们想做一期可以反复回味的节目，请上伊森和彭博新闻（Bloomberg News）的跨资产记者伊莎贝尔·李（Isabelle Lee），围绕其中几个主题和研究笔记做一期小小的聚焦专题。

turns.en: Yeah, so Athanasios is, in my opinion, the best chartist on the team. He also is, he comes up with the things that end up in my PowerPoints, I think the most. And the things where I'm like, oh, I didn't know that. So I think just like basically having one week where we just look at his stuff, I think is really worthwhile. The other thing is he doesn't like to do media.
turns.zh: 是的，在我看来，阿萨纳西奥斯是团队里最擅长做图表的人。他挖出来的东西，我认为是最后被我放进PPT里最多的，也是那些让我感叹'哦，我原来不知道'的东西。所以我觉得专门用一周时间来看他的研究成果，是非常值得的。另外还有一点，他不喜欢上媒体。

turns.en: He hates it.
turns.zh: 他很讨厌这个。

turns.en: I like forcing him to do media and that's fun for me. So those two things combined, I'm like, I think we should just sort of go through some of his notes and some of the things he found because he doesn't he's in the in the mines, man. He is like deep down in there. And so he surfaces some stuff that's like, whoa.
turns.zh: 我就喜欢逼着他上媒体，这对我来说很有乐趣。所以这两点加起来，我就想，我们真该过一遍他的一些研究笔记和他发现的东西，因为他……他是真的在矿井里挖啊，伙计。他就像深深扎在里面。所以他挖出来的一些东西会让人惊叹'哇'。

turns.en: OK, so let's start with one, Isabel. You like that or no? What's what's the one that that popped for you the most?
turns.zh: 好，那我们从其中一个开始吧。伊莎贝尔，你喜不喜欢？哪一个最让你眼前一亮？

turns.en: I have to say that Athanasius' research, we also like it in print, but we never tell him that because we don't want him too arrogant, you know? So we got to keep him.
turns.zh: 我得说，阿萨纳西奥斯的研究，我们在文字报道这边也很喜欢，但我们从来不告诉他，因为不想让他太自负，你懂吧？所以我们得让他保持——

turns.en: Grounded and humble. I'm enough. Yeah, they're like, we don't need another Eric running around here.
turns.zh: ——脚踏实地和谦逊。有我一个就够了。是的，他们那意思是'我们这儿可不需要再多一个埃里克到处晃悠'。

turns.en: We always say, wow, this is good amongst us, but we never tell it to him.
turns.zh: 我们私下里总会说'哇，这个真棒'，但从来不当面告诉他。

turns.en: In fact, we tell him- They like him because he's an anti-clout chaser.
turns.zh: 事实上我们还跟他说——大家喜欢他，恰恰是因为他是个'反蹭热度者'（anti-clout chaser）。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊。

turns.en: Whereas I'm like a total clout chaser. No kidding.
turns.zh: 而我呢，完全是个爱蹭热度的人，这可不假。

turns.en: There's no typo.
turns.zh: 一点没说错。

turns.en: Ooh, anti-clout.
turns.zh: 哦，'反蹭热度'。

turns.en: I like this.
turns.zh: 我喜欢这个说法。

turns.en: What do I like the most? The 80-20. We actually wrote a story on it.
turns.zh: 我最喜欢哪一个？是那个80/20。我们其实还专门为此写过一篇报道。

turns.en: So let's talk about this.
turns.zh: 那我们就来聊聊这个。

turns.en: Forever. Forever. has been the ratio you're supposed to use to build a portfolio. Ethan, 80-20, what is that?
turns.zh: 一直以来，60/40都是大家构建投资组合时应当采用的经典比例。伊森，那80/20又是怎么回事？

turns.en: Yeah, well, I'm glad to be up from the trenches. Be careful, we.
turns.zh: 是啊，嗯，很高兴能从'战壕'里冒个头。小心点，我们……

turns.en: Can send you right back down. We can, we can.
turns.zh: ……随时可以把你再送回下去。可以的，可以的。

turns.en: But the 80-20, okay, so obviously the normal default portfolio is.
turns.zh: 至于80/20，好，那么显然，传统的默认投资组合是——

turns.en: 60-40, right?

But stocks have been on this tremendous run. You have bonds that people really sort of soured on a little bit. So if we look at the breakdown of ETF assets, which used to be closer to 60-40, it's now like 80% in stocks, 20% in bonds. So I think people don't realize that you have a very heavy equity portfolio than we used to. You have things like buffers and covered calls, a lot of things that have sort of stepped into the bond role. So I think it's just this really negative sort of perception on bonds, right? And rates are going up.
turns.zh: 但股票一直处在这轮强劲的涨势里。而债券呢，大家其实有点对它失去了兴趣。所以如果我们看看ETF资产的构成，过去更接近60/40，现在大概是80%在股票、20%在债券。所以我觉得人们没有意识到，如今的股票仓位比以往要重得多。还有像缓冲型（buffer）ETF和备兑看涨（covered call）ETF这类产品，很多东西其实已经顶替了债券的角色。所以我认为，这纯粹是市场对债券有一种非常负面的看法，对吧？而且利率还在往上走。

turns.en: Shouldn't that incentivize people to get into the bonds?
turns.zh: 那这难道不应该反而激励人们去配置债券吗？

turns.en: I think if you're contrarian, this is a really interesting time. But I think overall, you're just very much more exposed to stocks than we've ever been in the past.
turns.zh: 我觉得，如果你是个逆向投资者，现在确实是个非常有意思的时点。但总体而言，我们对股票的风险敞口比以往任何时候都要大得多。

turns.en: Is the 20% composition bonds, or is it different than what you would have seen in the 60-40 composition?
turns.zh: 那20%的部分是由债券构成的吗？还是说它和你在60/40组合里看到的构成不一样？

turns.en: Yeah, that's the bond part. But I think maybe people are opening more up to alternatives, whether they're putting it in crypto or in some other bond alternatives. So maybe they still are looking for some sort of cushion, but they're just not using bonds anymore.
turns.zh: 是的，那部分就是债券。但我觉得人们可能越来越愿意接受另类资产（alternatives），不管是投到加密货币里，还是其他一些债券替代品。所以也许他们仍在寻找某种缓冲垫，只是不再用债券来实现而已。

turns.en: But you also make the point in your note that the 80% is a huge part of that is stock price appreciation. So it's not really by choice.
turns.zh: 但你在研究笔记里也指出，这80%中有很大一部分是源于股价的上涨。所以这并不完全是投资者主动选择的结果。

turns.en: No, definitely.
turns.zh: 对，确实如此。

turns.en: But I think people aren't rebalancing either, like selling it and going into bonds. I think they're just riding the equity wave.
turns.zh: 但我觉得人们也没有去做再平衡（rebalance），比如卖出股票转投债券。我认为他们只是在顺着这波股票涨势随波逐流。

turns.en: The percent of total assets that bond ETFs make up is 15%. It's not even 40 or 20. It's 15.
turns.zh: 债券ETF占总资产的比例是15%。既不是40，也不是20，而是15。

turns.en: And I'm with you. I think buffers and alternatives have stepped in there. And they are now the 5%. And so that's the modern portfolio.
turns.zh: 我同意你的看法。我觉得缓冲型产品和另类资产已经补位进来了，它们现在占了那5%。所以这才是现代版的投资组合。

turns.en: But the other thing is, if you look at the aggregate bond index, it has not kept up with inflation. Like the real return is negative a little bit. And now with rates going up, all the bonds that everybody holds in these funds, when rates go up, they're immediately worth less. So like all the bond funds are like now worth less.
turns.zh: 但另一方面，如果你看综合债券指数（aggregate bond index），它并没有跑赢通胀，也就是说实际回报率（real return）略微为负。而现在随着利率上升，大家在这些基金里持有的所有债券，一旦利率上行，立刻就不值钱了。所以所有的债券基金现在的价值都在缩水。

turns.en: So I'm with you. Maybe after yields top off, we could see some new launches.
turns.zh: 所以我同意你的看法。也许等收益率见顶之后，我们会看到一些新产品的发行。

turns.en: What I am interested in also is the money market mutual funds are not part of your data. And I do think a lot of people have moved money there. So if you add in money market mutual funds, it might be closer to 2030. But if you call those bonds, I mean, I guess that's cash. But those have like $ 8 trillion. And now with rates climbing, I think they could even get more. Because why don't I get my 5% in no risk rather than going out on.
turns.zh: 我还感兴趣的一点是，货币市场共同基金（money market mutual funds）并不在你的数据里。而我确实认为很多人已经把资金挪到了那里。所以如果把货币市场共同基金算进来，这个比例可能更接近20%到30%。但如果你把这些也算作债券的话……我是说，我猜那应该算现金。但这类基金规模大约有8万亿美元。而现在随着利率攀升，我觉得它们可能还会吸引更多资金。因为既然能毫无风险地拿到5%的收益，我为什么还要去冒险，沿着——

turns.en: The curve and taking my chance of the TLT, the widowmaker? I think that's what a lot of people will do.
turns.zh: ——收益率曲线往外走，去赌TLT（那个'寡妇制造者'）呢？我觉得很多人都会这么做。

turns.en: I'm surprised you said money market funds and not ETFs.
turns.zh: 我很惊讶你说的是货币市场基金，而不是货币市场ETF。

turns.en: Well, because the difference between.
turns.zh: 嗯，因为两者之间的区别在于——

turns.en: When you say cash or money market mutual fund, what people love about that is the NAV is $ 1 all the time. People just, especially institutions, they love to know that they can never lose money. In ETF, you cannot guarantee that. The NAVs do float. Even if they barely move, they move. And so that's a big difference, and you can never, ever have that in an ETF. So there is, again, there's a couple things here and there that can't be ETFized, and a stable $ 1 NAV is one of them, and that's why those funds will still get money, even though the mutual fund is largely rejected.
turns.zh: 当你说现金或货币市场共同基金时，人们喜欢它的一点在于它的净值（NAV）永远都是1美元。大家，尤其是机构投资者，就是喜欢知道他们永远不会亏钱。而在ETF里，你没法保证这一点，ETF的净值是会浮动的。哪怕它们几乎不动，那也是动的。所以这是一个很大的区别，你在ETF里永远、永远无法做到这一点。所以，同样地，市场里总有那么几样东西是没法'ETF化'（ETFized）的，而稳定的1美元净值就是其中之一，这也是为什么即便共同基金这种形式在很大程度上已经被抛弃，这类基金仍然能吸引到资金。

turns.en: Okay, next segment. It would be very difficult to do anything about investing now and not talk about the elephant in the room, which is U.S. midterms. That's not that far away. But some of your research has been not about the midterms necessarily, but about flows and political themed ETFs. What'd you learn?
turns.zh: 好，进入下一个环节。现在要聊投资，却不去谈那头'房间里的大象'（显而易见却被回避的话题），是很难的——那就是美国中期选举（midterms）。它已经不远了。但你的一些研究其实并不一定是关于中期选举本身，而是关于资金流向和政治主题ETF的。你从中发现了什么？

turns.en: There's two main ones out there. There's one that tracks sort of what the Republican Party is buying, and there's one on the Democratic Party.
turns.zh: 市面上主要有两只。有一只是追踪共和党（Republican）方面在买什么的，还有一只是关于民主党（Democratic）的。

turns.en: One has a ticker that is GOP. You can guess which one that is. And the other one is? Is Nance. N-A-N-C. That's so cool.
turns.zh: 有一只的代码（ticker）是GOP，你猜得到是哪一只。另一只呢？是NANC，N-A-N-C。这太酷了。

turns.en: I may be behind that, because remember when Nancy.
turns.zh: 这事儿背后可能就有我的功劳，因为还记得当年南希（Nancy）——

turns.en: Pelosi's portfolio was going viral and Litquidity was tweeting about it, this was like eight, nine years ago. I kept saying, I'm surprised somebody doesn't launch Nance. But this isn't just her portfolio.
turns.zh: ——佩洛西（Pelosi）的投资组合在网上疯传、Litquidity还在发推追踪它的时候，那大概是八九年前了。我一直说，我很惊讶居然没有人推出一只'NANC'。但这只ETF追踪的并不只是她一个人的组合。

turns.en: I have to get a fat check on this.
turns.zh: 那我真得为这个领一大笔奖金。

turns.en: This is your Hall of Fame and Diet Arc, Eric.
turns.zh: 这可是属于你的'名人堂'（Hall of Fame）高光时刻啊，埃里克。

turns.en: If you go into Twitter and you search for hashtag Nance, I believe my tweet will be the first thing you see if you went.
turns.zh: 如果你上Twitter（推特）搜索话题标签#NANC，我相信你看到的第一条就会是我的推文，如果你回到——

turns.en: Back in time. And then if you remember the whole thing with Grift from Tuttle that never ended up launching.
turns.zh: ——过去去搜的话。然后，如果你还记得Tuttle资本（Tuttle Capital）那只'Grift'ETF的整件事——它最终并没能成功发行。

turns.en: I like how he makes this podcast that's about you about him.
turns.zh: 我就服了他——硬是把这档节目聊成了关于他自己的。

turns.en: Grift never launched. Last time I talked to him, I think he's looking for a home.
turns.zh: 'Grift'始终没能发行。上次我和他聊的时候，我记得他还在为它找个'落脚的地方'。

turns.en: Oh, yeah. He's still trying to figure that out. We've back tested it and kind of tried to figure out what it would look like.
turns.zh: 哦，对，他还在琢磨这事儿。我们对它做过回测（back test），也大致试着搞清楚它会是什么样子。

turns.en: But we've looked at.
turns.zh: 不过我们研究了——

turns.en: Performance of Nance and GOP. And as you can imagine, when there was a Democratic president, Nance was doing better. And now GOP is doing slightly better. But I think where it gets interesting is there are names that are held by both.
turns.zh: ——NANC和GOP的表现。可想而知，当总统是民主党人时，NANC表现更好；而现在GOP略胜一筹。但我觉得真正有意思的地方在于，有一些股票是两党都持有的。

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: So I know everyone wants to sort of like politicize everything.
turns.zh: 我知道大家都想把什么都政治化。

turns.en: Wait, there's a middle?
turns.zh: 等等，还有中间地带？

turns.en: Yeah, there's some stocks like Intel, Amazon, CrowdStrike that actually both parties hold. And if you were to just build a basket of those, you end up beating everything.
turns.zh: 是的，有一些股票，比如英特尔（Intel）、亚马逊（Amazon）、CrowdStrike，其实是两党都持有的。而如果你就把这些股票打包成一个组合，最后它会跑赢所有其他组合。

turns.en: Now, when you say that both parties hold, is this things that the lawmakers themselves hold or that there's this commonality?
turns.zh: 那么，当你说两党都持有时，指的是议员们本人持有的股票，还是说存在这样一种共同性？

turns.en: Let me step in here.
turns.zh: 让我来插一句。

turns.en: These two ETFs track what the lawmakers are buying and selling in their personal portfolio, which makes a lot of sense because I'm not going to say they have inside information, but they certainly have a lot of information about what's going on with companies. So there is a cynicism to these ETFs. The Grift ETF, I think, was going to be on stuff the White House invested in. That's a whole other level, which I still think that would make a good ETF. These, to me, are better than the ones that are like donations and stuff because these are like, hey, look, these people have good information.
turns.zh: 这两只ETF追踪的是议员们在个人投资组合里买卖的股票，这非常有道理——因为我不想说他们掌握了内幕信息（inside information），但他们无疑对各家公司的动向掌握着大量信息。所以这类ETF是带有一种'犬儒'色彩的。而那只'Grift'ETF，我记得本来是要追踪白宫方面投资的东西，那完全是另一个层次了，我至今仍然觉得那会是只好ETF。在我看来，这两只要比那些追踪政治捐款之类的ETF更好，因为它们的逻辑是'嘿，看，这些人掌握着优质信息'。

turns.en: Don't you want to learn what– ride their coattails?
turns.zh: 你难道不想学学他们、搭他们的顺风车（ride their coattails）吗？

turns.en: And if they both like a stock, I just think you know it's good. Because you don't agree on anything. But they agree on Intel.
turns.zh: 而且如果他们两党都喜欢某只股票，我就会觉得，你知道，这股票肯定不错。因为你们（两党）在其他任何事上都无法认同彼此，但他们在英特尔（Intel）上却达成了一致。

turns.en: Behind the closed doors. Let's all just be clear. Amazon's good.
turns.zh: 关起门来之后，咱们就把话说明白：亚马逊是好股票。

turns.en: Yeah, we like that.
turns.zh: 是的，我们喜欢这个。

turns.en: I think in general, sure, these are all politically laced ETFs. Add in MAGA of Yorkville and YOL, which Yorkville also acquired. I don't think any of these have substantial assets. So to an extent, I feel like people like to talk about politics. But when it comes to actually investing, they become a little bit more Less emotional. Let's say less emotional. You know, none of these.
turns.zh: 我觉得总体而言，没错，这些都是带有浓厚政治色彩的ETF。再加上Yorkville旗下的MAGA，以及同样被Yorkville收购的YOL。我不觉得这些基金里有任何一只拥有可观的资产规模。所以在某种程度上，我感觉人们喜欢谈论政治，但一到真金白银投资的时候，他们就会变得稍微……不那么情绪化一些。就说不那么情绪化吧。你知道的，这些基金没有一只——

turns.en: Have huge assets. And forever have been unwilling to actually put the money into them.
turns.zh: ——拥有巨大的资产规模。而且大家一直都不愿意真正把钱投进去。

turns.en: You got to separate these.
turns.zh: 你得把这些区分开来看。

turns.en: MAGA and Y'all are about which stocks the GOP donates to. And they tend to be heavy energy and like CEOs that are Republican.
turns.zh: MAGA和YOL关注的是共和党的政治捐款流向了哪些股票。这类持仓往往偏重能源板块，以及那些CEO是共和党人的公司。

turns.en: Fair.
turns.zh: 有道理。

turns.en: That's sort of the anti-ESG. I think both of the sides are there as like not really working.
turns.zh: 那算是'反ESG'（anti-ESG）的产品。我觉得这两边的（政治主题）基金表现都不算成功。

turns.en: These are purely like, hey, these people have access to information we don't have. And you know they love to trade and gamble. And they love their stocks. So why don't we just buy what they're buying? It's almost like a 13F tracking ETF.
turns.zh: 而这两只（NANC和GOP）纯粹就是'嘿，这些人能接触到我们接触不到的信息，而且你知道他们喜欢交易和投机，也钟爱自己的股票，那我们何不直接买他们在买的东西？'这几乎就像是一只追踪13F（机构持仓披露文件）的ETF。

turns.en: I see your point. That said, why are assets not substantial?
turns.zh: 我明白你的意思。话虽如此，为什么这些基金的资产规模并不可观呢？

turns.en: Well, Nance has $ 300 million.
turns.zh: 嗯，NANC有3亿美元的规模。

turns.en: That's pretty good.
turns.zh: 那已经挺不错了。

turns.en: Pretty good. It's not great.
turns.zh: 挺不错，但也算不上出色。

turns.en: Yeah, I agree.
turns.zh: 是啊，我同意。

turns.en: No offense to Nance and GOP.
turns.zh: 无意冒犯NANC和GOP这两只基金。

turns.en: I think GOP is smaller.
turns.zh: 我记得GOP的规模更小一些。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: I get it, they're kind of novelty ETFs in a way. I think people maybe just want to look at them, but not necessarily buy them.
turns.zh: 我懂，它们在某种程度上算是'新奇型'（novelty）ETF。我觉得大家可能只是想看看它们，但不一定会真的去买。

turns.en: There's hope for bipartisanship. Maybe. Make up a ticker, Joel.
turns.zh: 看来两党合作（bipartisanship）还是有希望的，也许吧。乔尔，你倒是编个代码出来啊。

turns.en: For an issuer, if Nance has $ 300 million and it charges 70 basis points.
turns.zh: 对发行商来说，如果NANC有3亿美元规模、收费70个基点（basis points），

turns.en: Yes, that's fair.
turns.zh: 是的，这说得通。

turns.en: That's the equivalent of a billion dollar ETF that charges 30 basis points.
turns.zh: 那就相当于一只规模10亿美元、收费30个基点的ETF（所带来的收入）。

turns.en: It's not nothing, that's for sure. Yeah, it's not nothing, but I agree. It's a speck of sand in the ETF world. Vanguard takes in $ 300 million by the time we just talked about this.
turns.zh: 这可不是小数目，那是肯定的。是的，不算小，但我同意——放在整个ETF世界里，它就是一粒沙。就在我们刚才聊这天的工夫，先锋领航（Vanguard）就已经进账3亿美元了。

turns.en: All right, last segment for this episode. We're just ending September before we start. recording, we were all talking about how September sucks. But you actually did research, Ethan, that backs that up for real. Because forever, September is sort of like not a great month for returns. Yeah.
turns.zh: 好，这是本期的最后一个环节。我们正好赶在九月底（录制）。开始录音之前，我们都在吐槽九月有多糟糕。但伊森，你还真做了研究来实锤这一点。因为一直以来，九月在回报方面都算不上一个好月份。是的。

turns.en: It's usually, I think, like the worst month of the year, which you'd kind of think it'd be.
turns.zh: 我觉得它通常是一年里最糟糕的月份，虽然你本来会以为它应该是个——

turns.en: Good month.
turns.zh: 好月份。

turns.en: But I think it's just there's this summer lull. People come back. The market is up. It tends and people end up selling a lot in September, just kind of taking profits before the year end. But through the ETF lens, September is like the busiest month for launches. Flows don't really get derailed just because the market's down. I think we're a little flat this year in September. But yeah, it just ends up being a really, really bad month seasonality wise. And yeah, that seems to be coming to fruition this year. It's just kind of been a pretty dull month.
turns.zh: 但我觉得只是因为有个夏季的淡季（summer lull）。人们休假回来，市场又涨了一波，于是大家往往会在九月大量卖出，赶在年底前落袋为安（take profits）。不过如果从ETF的角度看，九月反而是新基金发行最繁忙的月份。资金流向并不会仅仅因为市场下跌就脱轨。我觉得今年九月我们大概持平。但没错，从季节性（seasonality）来看，九月最终就是个非常非常糟糕的月份。是的，今年似乎也应验了，这一个月一直相当沉闷。

turns.en: Let me just say this about the launches. I think when people come back and their eyeballs are on the markets.
turns.zh: 关于新基金发行，我就说一点。我觉得当人们休假回来、目光重新盯在市场上的时候，

turns.en: Come back from summer vacations.
turns.zh: 就是从暑期休假回来的时候。

turns.en: Yeah, that's when people like to launch. And I do think that it would take more than a bad month or two for these launches to slow down.
turns.zh: 对，那正是大家愿意发行新产品的时候。而且我确实认为，要让这波发行潮慢下来，光靠一两个糟糕的月份是不够的。

turns.en: I think, you know, Ethan says it. We all say it in the team sometimes. We need a hard rain. And like, you know, a flat month is not a hard rain. So I just don't think anything is going to slow down.
turns.zh: 我觉得，你知道的，伊森常这么说，我们团队里有时也都会说：我们需要一场'暴雨'（a hard rain，意指一次真正的市场重挫）。而一个持平的月份可算不上暴雨。所以我不觉得任何事情会慢下来。

turns.en: I think issuers are getting FOMO now. Like they want to be first. So they're not waiting for a month. Like if they want to get something out right away, it doesn't matter what month it is. They're just going to try to get it out.
turns.zh: 我觉得发行商现在正陷入'错失恐惧症'（FOMO）。他们都想抢第一个。所以他们不会为了等某个月份而观望。如果他们想马上推出一只产品，那不管是几月都无所谓，他们就是会想办法把它推出来。

turns.en: What's going to bring the hard rain?
turns.zh: 那什么才会带来那场'暴雨'呢？

turns.en: I wrote a note recently about bond mutual funds. To me, this is the canary in the coal mine to watch for something breaking. Because as yields go up, these boomers who own these bond mutual.
turns.zh: 我最近写了一篇关于债券型共同基金（bond mutual funds）的笔记。在我看来，这是观察'某个环节是否会崩断'的'矿井里的金丝雀'（canary in the coal mine，即预警信号）。因为随着收益率上升，那些持有这些债券型共同基金的'婴儿潮一代'（boomers）——

turns.en: Funds, they're very fickle. If the NAV starts going down, because a lot.
turns.zh: ——他们其实很善变。一旦净值（NAV）开始下跌，因为很多——

turns.en: Of these bond funds hold bonds that are worthless, so their NAVs are lower, they have to force sell bonds, which will make yields go even higher.
turns.zh: ——这类债券基金持有的债券其实已经不值钱了，所以它们的净值更低；他们不得不被迫抛售债券，而这又会让收益率进一步走高。

turns.en: It's like a doom loop.
turns.zh: 这就像一个'死亡循环'（doom loop）。

turns.en: And as yields go higher, their bonds are worth even less.
turns.zh: 而随着收益率走高，他们的债券就更不值钱了。

turns.en: The NAV goes down.
turns.zh: 净值随之下跌。

turns.en: There's more outflows. We saw this happen a couple of times in 2020 and 2022.
turns.zh: 于是有更多的资金流出（outflows）。我们在2020年和2022年就见过这种情况发生过好几次。

turns.en: And it can get bad.
turns.zh: 而且情况可能会变得很糟。

turns.en: And these outflows can really start to pick up. And I think that's something to watch. That is where I think something could break is in the bond mutual fund area. It's sparking a doom loop with the 4.5 trillion they have in assets. That's public information. It's something we can watch. And they have to sell the bonds. When they see outflows, they've got to get rid of them. And I think it's going to be interesting that Most of the time that government steps in, when you're talking about inflation, if inflation is the issue, you can't step in as easily because if you step in and throw money at the problem, as usual, that could make inflation worse. So inflation kind of makes the government intervention maybe a little, it's going to have to get more extreme.
turns.zh: 而这些资金流出真的可能开始加速。我觉得这是值得关注的一点。我认为可能'崩断'的地方，就在债券型共同基金这一块。它们手中掌握着4.5万亿美元的资产，一旦触发，就会点燃一个'死亡循环'。这些都是公开信息，是我们能够观察的。而他们不得不卖出债券——一旦看到资金流出，他们就必须把债券脱手。我觉得有意思的是，大多数时候政府都会出手干预，但当你谈论的是通胀时，如果问题恰恰是通胀，政府就没那么容易介入了，因为如果像往常那样出手、往问题里砸钱，反而可能让通胀更严重。所以通胀在某种程度上会让政府干预……嗯，事态可能得先恶化到更极端的地步（政府才会出手）。

turns.en: But I don't know. I personally, I've seen this movie.
turns.zh: 但我也说不好。就我个人而言，这部'电影'我已经看过了（意指类似的戏码我见多了）。

turns.en: I just don't get too worried anymore until I see like, I want to see more outflows, more carnage.
turns.zh: 我已经不会再太担心了，除非我看到——我想看到更多的资金流出、更多的'血流成河'（carnage），才会当真。

turns.en: He's watching the weather report and being like, eh, it hasn't started raining yet.
turns.zh: 他就像在看天气预报，然后说'呃，还没开始下雨呢'。

turns.en: I know.
turns.zh: 我知道。

turns.en: He always says around COVID, I was the guy from Jaws who was like, the beaches are fine.
turns.zh: 他就爱说，新冠那阵子他就是《大白鲨》（Jaws）里那个角色，一直念叨'海滩没事的'。

turns.en: The mayor.
turns.zh: 就是那个市长。

turns.en: If the flood doesn't reach your head, you're fine. Wait, I'm curious, actually.
turns.zh: '只要洪水没淹到你头顶，你就没事。'等等，其实我挺好奇的——

turns.en: It's just the flu.
turns.zh: '不就是场流感嘛。'

turns.en: It's just the flu. I'm curious when the month where we see most closures, because you did say September is strong.
turns.zh: '不就是场流感嘛。'我好奇的是，哪个月份我们会看到最多的基金清盘（closures）？因为你确实说过九月很强劲。

turns.en: Oh, that's a good one.
turns.zh: 哦，这是个好问题。

turns.en: I don't know.
turns.zh: 我不太确定。

turns.en: I think it's towards the end of the year because they're kind of like rationalizing their lineups before the end of the year.
turns.zh: 我觉得是在接近年底的时候，因为发行商往往会在年底前精简（rationalize）自己的产品线。

turns.en: All right. Athanasios, Isabel, thanks for joining us on Trillions.
turns.zh: 好的。阿萨纳西奥斯、伊莎贝尔，感谢你们做客《万亿》。

turns.en: Thank you.
turns.zh: 谢谢。

turns.en: Thanks for having me back. Yeah, sure.
turns.zh: 谢谢你们再次邀请我。嗯，当然。

turns.en: Thanks for listening to Trillions. Until next time, you can find us on the Bloomberg Terminal, Bloomberg.com, Apple Podcasts, Spotify, or wherever else you like to listen. We'd love to hear from you. Hit us up. Trillions is produced by Magnus Henriksen and Keshav Pandya. Amy Keene is our executive producer. Cheryl Brumley is the head of Bloomberg Podcasts. Bye.
turns.zh: 感谢收听《万亿》。下期再见之前，你可以在彭博终端（Bloomberg Terminal）、Bloomberg.com、Apple Podcasts、Spotify，或任何你喜欢的收听平台上找到我们。我们很乐意听到你的反馈，欢迎联系我们。《万亿》由马格努斯·亨利克森（Magnus Henriksen）和凯沙夫·潘迪亚（Keshav Pandya）制作，艾米·基恩（Amy Keene）担任执行制作人，谢丽尔·布鲁姆利（Cheryl Brumley）是彭博播客（Bloomberg Podcasts）负责人。再见。
